lessons.title: DOM Manipulation
lessons.html:
DOM Manipulation Fundamentals

The Document Object Model (DOM) represents HTML as a tree structure. JavaScript can read/modify this tree dynamically without page reload.

Selecting Elements:

  • document.getElementById('id') - By ID (fastest)
  • document.querySelector('.class') - First match CSS selector
  • document.querySelectorAll('tag') - All matches
<button id="myBtn">Click me</button>
<div id="output"></div>
const btn = document.getElementById('myBtn');
const output = document.getElementById('output');

btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    output.textContent = 'Button clicked!';
    output.style.color = 'blue';
    output.style.fontSize = '20px';
});

Practice: Create counter button that changes background color randomly.

Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding the fundamental concepts is crucial for advanced topics
  • Always consider edge cases and error handling in production code
  • Practice with real-world examples to solidify your knowledge

lessons.title: Event Handling
lessons.html:
Advanced Event Handling

Events make websites interactive. Use addEventListener for modern event handling.

Common Events:

EventWhen triggered
clickMouse click
inputAny form input change
submitForm submission
keydownKey pressed
mouseoverMouse enters element
const form = document.querySelector('form');
form.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();  // Stop form submission
    const name = document.getElementById('name').value;
    const email = document.getElementById('email').value;
    alert(`Welcome, ${name}! Email: ${email}`);
});

Event Object Properties: e.target, e.key, e.preventDefault()

lessons.title: ES6+ Modern Features
lessons.html:
ES6+ JavaScript Features

Modern JavaScript (ES6+) makes code shorter, readable, and powerful.

1. Arrow Functions:

// Old way
function add(a, b) {
    return a + b;
}

// Arrow function
const add = (a, b) => a + b;

// With block
const multiply = (a, b) => {
    console.log(`Multiplying ${a} * ${b}`);
    return a * b;
};

2. Destructuring:

const person = { name: 'Alice', age: 30, city: 'NY' };
const { name, age } = person;  // Extract properties
console.log(`${name} is ${age}`);

// Array destructuring
const [first, second] = ['apple', 'banana'];

lessons.title: Async JavaScript
lessons.html:
Asynchronous Programming

JavaScript handles async operations with Promises and async/await. Perfect for API calls.

Fetch API + Promises:

fetch('https://api.github.com/users/octocat')
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(user => {
    document.body.innerHTML += `<h2>${user.name}</h2><p>${user.bio}</p>`;
  })
  .catch(error => console.error('Error:', error));

Cleaner async/await:

async function getUser() {
    try {
        const response = await fetch('https://api.github.com/users/octocat');
        const user = await response.json();
        console.log(`${user.login} - ${user.public_repos} repos`);
    } catch (error) {
        console.error('Failed to fetch user');
    }
}

lessons.title: LocalStorage
lessons.html:
Client-Side Data Storage

Store data directly in browser. No server needed!

localStorage (Permanent):

// Save data
localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
localStorage.setItem('user', JSON.stringify({
    name: 'Alice',
    preferences: { notifications: true }
}));

// Load data
const theme = localStorage.getItem('theme');
const user = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('user'));
console.log(user.name, user.preferences.notifications);

sessionStorage (Current session):

sessionStorage.setItem('tempCart', JSON.stringify(items));

Warning: Max 5-10MB. Never store passwords!

lessons.title: ES Modules
lessons.html:
JavaScript Modules

Split code into reusable files. Import/export between files.

math.js:

export const PI = 3.14159;

export function circleArea(r) {
    return PI * r * r;
}

export default class Circle {
    constructor(radius) { this.radius = radius; }
    area() { return circleArea(this.radius); }
}

main.js:

import Circle, { PI, circleArea } from './math.js';

const c = new Circle(5);
console.log(c.area());  // 78.54
console.log(PI);  // 3.14159

lessons.title: Todo App Project
lessons.html:
Complete Todo Application

Combine all concepts: DOM, events, localStorage, modules!

Features:

  • Add/delete tasks
  • Mark complete
  • Persist data
  • Filter tasks
class TodoApp {
    constructor() {
        this.todos = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('todos')) || [];
        this.render();
    }

    addTask(text) {
        this.todos.push({
            id: Date.now(),
            text,
            completed: false,
            created: new Date().toISOString()
        });
        this.save();
        this.render();
    }

    save() {
        localStorage.setItem('todos', JSON.stringify(this.todos));
    }
}

lessons.title: Fetch API & HTTP Requests
lessons.html:
Making HTTP Requests

The Fetch API provides a modern interface for making HTTP requests from the browser.

GET Requests:

async function getUsers() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/users', {
      method: 'GET',
      headers: {
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${getToken()}`
      }
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
    }

    const users = await response.json();
    return users;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to fetch users:', error);
    throw error;
  }
}

POST and Other Methods:

async function createUser(userData) {
  const response = await fetch('/api/users', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(userData),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const error = await response.json();
    throw new Error(error.message || 'Failed to create user');
  }

  return await response.json();
}

// PUT request
async function updateUser(id, userData) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'PUT',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(userData),
  });
  return await response.json();
}

// DELETE request
async function deleteUser(id) {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
  });
  return response.status === 204;  // No content
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Build a REST client with all CRUD operations
  2. Add request retry logic for network failures
  3. Implement request cancellation with AbortController

Key Takeaways:

  • Fetch returns a Promise that resolves to Response
  • Always check response.ok before parsing body
  • Errors should be caught and handled gracefully

lessons.title: CSS Animations & Transitions
lessons.html:
CSS Animations and Transitions

CSS animations bring web pages to life with smooth transitions and keyframe animations.

CSS Transitions:

/* Transition: property duration easing-function delay */
.button {
  background-color: blue;
  color: white;
  padding: 10px 20px;
  transition: background-color 0.3s ease, transform 0.2s ease;
}

.button:hover {
  background-color: darkblue;
  transform: scale(1.05);
}

/* Fade in */
.modal {
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out;
}

.modal.active {
  opacity: 1;
}

/* Slide down */
.dropdown {
  max-height: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: max-height 0.3s ease-out;
}

.dropdown.open {
  max-height: 500px;
}

Keyframe Animations:

@keyframes slideIn {
  from {
    transform: translateX(-100%);
    opacity: 0;
  }
  to {
    transform: translateX(0);
    opacity: 1;
  }
}

@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% {
    transform: scale(1);
  }
  50% {
    transform: scale(1.1);
  }
}

@keyframes spin {
  0% { transform: rotate(0deg); }
  100% { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}

.animated-element {
  animation: slideIn 0.5s ease-out forwards;
}

.loader {
  width: 40px;
  height: 40px;
  border: 4px solid #f3f3f3;
  border-top: 4px solid blue;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin 1s linear infinite;
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a fade-in page transition effect
  2. Build a loading spinner component
  3. Implement a slide-in notification system

Key Takeaways:

  • Transitions smooth property changes over time
  • Keyframes define multi-step animations
  • GPU-accelerated properties (transform, opacity) perform best
